gaps.lead: The suitcase was so heavy that I couldn't lift it.
gaps.sentence: It was ___ that I couldn't lift it.
gaps.explanation: so + adjective + that → such (+a) + adjective + noun + that.

gaps.lead: 'Why don't we hold the wedding outdoors?' said Ana.
gaps.explanation: suggest + that-clause, or suggest + -ing: suggested they hold / suggested holding.

gaps.lead: He no longer thinks he can find a job before the end of the year.
gaps.sentence: He has given ___ a job before the end of the year.
gaps.explanation: 'No longer thinks he can find' becomes 'has given up hope of finding'.

gaps.lead: Do you mind if I come over to see you later?
gaps.sentence: Do you ___ coming over to see you later?
gaps.explanation: 'Have any objection to me/my coming' is the formal equivalent of 'do you mind'.

gaps.lead: It's a pity I didn't bring my camera.
gaps.explanation: 'If only I had brought' expresses regret about the past.

gaps.lead: The garage is servicing my car tomorrow morning.
gaps.explanation: Arranged service: have/get something done — having my car serviced.
